newsitem.title: UK: Hanson Energy Group targets US aquisitions.
newsitem.headline: Hanson Energy Group targets US aquisitions.

text.p: The Energy Group, the last division to be spun off from conglomerate Hanson Plc, said on Tuesday at a press briefing it planned a spate of acquisitions, aiming for the U.S. market in particular once its split is complete.

In its listing details, released earlier, Energy said it was considering a number of opportunitites and had entered into "exclusive and confidential" talks with a U.S. power marketing company, subject to due diligence. It is also looking at possible deals in the generating sector in the U.S. and UK.

The group told the news briefing it planned to call on the U.S. Peabody coal division's knowledge of that market to help it identify opportunities which matched its existing assets, said Irl Engelhardt, the Peabody chief executive.

The Eastern group finance director Eric Anstee said the group would use the cash generated by the coal and network businesses and invest it where it saw earnings growth -- in the growing power sector.
Eastern generated a total of 354 million pounds in cash flow in the year ended September 30, he said.

Energy, which also owns the UK electricity distribution business Eastern, as well as the fourth largest electricity generator in the UK and a gas supply business, said that worldwide demand for energy was expected to rise by between 34 and 46 percent between 1993 and 2010.

World electricity output is, according to the US Department of Energy, expected to grow by 63 percent to 2010, with coal and gas accounting for 41 percent and 17 percent of that generation level by 2010.
Energy sees this, plus deregulation in world markets and privatisation, as the key opportunities for the group.
Energy is being sold with 1.4 billion stg of debt and has "A" rated credit from the rating agencies, said Derek Bonham, Energy group chief executive.
The group's last annual turnover was 3.6 billion, with pre-exceptional profits of 446 million stg. Total assets are 5.7 billion.
Bonham said the group, which is set to demerge on February 24, will be large enough to rank inside the FTSE 100 in the UK and the Fortune 500 in the U.S.
Investor roadshows are being planned on both sides of the Atlantic, with 35 percent of Hanson's shares held in the U.S.
The extraordinary general meeting on the demerger is due February 21. Shareholders will receive one Energy share for every 10 existing Hanson shares, a company statement said earlier.
